title: Necrotising soft-tissue infection recognition
logic: Soft-tissue infection with any of: pain out of proportion, oedema or tenderness extending beyond visible erythema, skin dusky/blistering/necrotic patches, crepitus, rapidly advancing edge, or systemic toxicity disproportionate to the visible wound
action: Critical alert: this is a surgical emergency, not an antibiotic titration problem — senior surgical review now, mark and time the advancing edge, resuscitate in parallel, theatre for radical debridement within hours; book the 12-24 h relook at the first operation

title: Circumferential deep burn threatening perfusion or ventilation
logic: Circumferential full-thickness burn of a limb with progressive pain, tightness, reduced distal perfusion or sensation — or of the chest with rising ventilation pressures/restricted excursion
action: Bedside escharotomy pathway immediately (longitudinal releasing incisions through eschar along standard lines, chest grid for ventilation restriction); do not transfer an unreleased circumferential burn; reassess perfusion after release and document

title: Flap or replant vascular compromise
logic: Post-operative flap/replant that is pale/white (arterial) or congested/purple with brisk dark bleeding (venous), cool, or with lost capillary refill signal
action: Immediate surgeon notification — salvage is measured in hours; loosen dressings/sutures at the bedside per protocol, ensure warmth, elevate for congestion or level for pallor, and prepare for return to theatre; never book flap concerns to the next routine round

title: Burn extent and depth assessment standard
logic: Burn recorded AND (%TBSA missing, or paediatric burn assessed without Lund-Browder, or depth not recorded) — erythema must be excluded from %TBSA
action: Require %TBSA (Lund-Browder chart for children, rule-of-nines acceptable for adults) and depth category at admission and at 48-72 h re-review (burns declare late); the %TBSA field drives fluid-resuscitation calculation and referral criteria

title: Burns referral-criteria screen
logic: Burn admission where any of: %TBSA over ~10% (adult) or ~5% (child), full-thickness component, involvement of face/hands/perineum/major joints, inhalational features, electrical or chemical mechanism, or extremes of age — and no burns-unit referral recorded
action: Surface the referral checklist and require either a referral record or a documented senior decision to manage locally; inhalational features additionally trigger early airway assessment

title: Tetanus and antimicrobial policy for contaminated soft-tissue wounds
logic: Burn, crush, bite or contaminated soft-tissue wound recorded AND tetanus prophylaxis status missing; systemic antibiotics recorded for a clean burn without infection signs
action: Require tetanus status on every such wound; conversely flag routine systemic antibiotic prophylaxis for burns (not indicated without infection or peri-operative context) — topical antimicrobials and excision policy are the infection strategy

title: Adjuvant plan mandatory for keloid excision
logic: Keloid excision listed AND no adjuvant therapy plan (serial intralesional corticosteroid schedule, pressure device, or radiotherapy referral) attached to the episode
action: Block listing until the adjuvant pathway and recurrence counselling are documented — excision alone recurs in the majority and often worse; auto-generate the post-excision steroid-injection appointment series

title: Graft and donor-site check schedule
logic: Split/full-thickness graft applied: first inspection due day 3-5 (earlier for soaking, odour, fever or pain spike); donor-site dressing retained 10-14 days
action: Schedule the day-3-5 graft take-down by trained staff with percentage-take recorded; unscheduled early take-down triggers infection review; haematoma/seroma found at inspection is evacuated and re-bolstered the same day; donor-site check booked at 10-14 days

title: Scar management and contracture surveillance after burns
logic: Healed deep burn or grafted burn crossing a joint AND no scar-programme enrolment (pressure garments, silicone, physiotherapy, splintage) or joint-range review booked
action: Enrol in the scar-management programme at wound closure with reviews at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months recording joint range and photographs; children remain under surveillance through growth; falling range between visits generates a contracture-release assessment

title: SCC margin chase and surveillance schedule
logic: Skin-cancer excision performed AND (histology result not linked within 4 weeks OR involved margins without a re-excision/radiotherapy plan OR no surveillance appointments booked)
action: Task the team to chase and link histology; involved margins auto-generate a re-excision listing decision; book risk-based surveillance (typically 3-6 monthly for 2 years) with node-basin examination at each visit; persons with albinism additionally enrolled in whole-skin surveillance and sun-protection supply
